name: An Ample Two-Vertex Completion of a Tree Is a Two-Apex Square Complex
statement: Let $B$ be ample and let distinct $u,v\in B$ satisfy that $G(B)-\{u,v\}$ is a nonempty tree. Every cube of dimension at least two is a square meeting $\{u,v\}$, no two squares have the same direction support, and the number of squares is $q(B)=\deg_B(u)+\deg_B(v)-\mathbf 1_{uv\in E(G(B))}-2$.
proof: A square avoiding both apices would be a cycle in the remaining tree. Every cube of dimension at least four has a square face avoiding two prescribed vertices; a three-cube either has an opposite square avoiding both or, when the apices are antipodal, leaves a six-cycle after their deletion. Thus only squares remain. The connected ample carrier of a fixed square support cannot contain two anchors, since consecutive anchors would create a three-cube, so supports are unique. With $r$ active directions, $n=|B|$, and $q$ squares, ampleness gives $n=1+r+q$ and the edge-shadow identity gives $|E(G(B))|=r+2q$. Restoring the apices to the $(n-2)$-vertex tree gives $|E(G(B))|=n-3+\deg(u)+\deg(v)-\mathbf 1_{uv\in E}$; substitution yields the formula.
